title: Second Nehru ministry adopts Decimalisation of Indian rupee and discontinue the concept of anna coin system.
text: The Indian rupee is the official currency of India and the erstwhile Dominion of India and British Raj. The rupee is subdivided into 100 paise (singular: paisa).

title: First elected government of Kerala. Communist Party of India won the elections and E. M. S. Namboodiripad became the first chief minister of united Kerala.
text: Kerala, officially Keralam, is a state on the Malabar Coast of southern India. It was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, which unified the country's Malayalam-speaking regions into a single state.

title: Indian Polo Team won the Polo World cup held at France.
text: Polo is a Mallet and ball game that is played on ponyback on an English style riding as a traditional field sport, and is one of the oldest known team sports in the world. Outdoor or "field" polo is played on a 300-by-160-yard grass field, while indoor or "arena" polo is played on a smaller 300-by-150-foot dirt arena.

title: Indian Air Force inducts its first jet bomber Canberra at Squadron 5, Agra.
text: A bomber is a military combat aircraft that utilizes air-to-ground weaponry to drop bombs, launch torpedoes, or deploy air-launched cruise missiles. There are two major classifications of bomber: strategic and tactical.

title: Hindustan Shipyard delivers its first passenger cum cargo vessel M V Andaman.
text: Hindustan Shipyard Limited is a public sector undertaking shipyard located in Visakhapatnam, on the east coast of India. HSL is a major shipyard in India, with a capacity to manufacture vessels up to 80,000 deadweight tonnage (DWT).

title: V. S. Wakankar discovers Bhimbetka rock shelter cave paintings.
text: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are an archaeological site in central India that spans the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods, as well as the historic period. It exhibits the earliest traces of human life in India and evidence of the Stone Age starting at the site in Acheulean times.

title: Balbir Singh Sr. became the first hockey player to be awarded the Padma Shri.
text: Balbir Singh Dosanjh predominantly known as Balbir Singh Sr., was an Indian hockey player and coach. He was a three-time Olympic gold medalist, having played a key role in India's wins in London (1948), Helsinki (1952) (as vice captain), and Melbourne (1956) (as captain) Olympics.
